clue.text: Stop batting at customs?

definitions.meaning: in cricket a captain may close the innings voluntarily, ending the side's batting
what a traveller does with dutiable goods at the customs desk: lists them officially

explanation.walkthrough: To declare in cricket (the British bat-and-ball game) is to end your side's innings early; at customs you declare goods you are bringing in.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of making a formal announcement: closing an innings, or listing goods for duty.

clue.text: See 13
Two-way cooker to throw away at island in lake, taking nearly nine days

indicators.note: in means the throwing away, at and island go inside the lake

parts.note: Como is a lake in northern Italy
to bin is to throw away

indicators.note: nearly drops the final letter of the nine days

parts.note: a novena is nine days of prayer

explanation.surface: A two-mode cooker gets binned at an island in a lake after nearly nine days.
explanation.definitionFit: This appliance works both as a microwave and a conventional oven, so it cooks in two ways.

clue.text: A large part of a saucy dish 20

indicators.note: only a large part is kept, the final letters of the dish being cut

parts.note: a fricassée is meat stewed in a white sauce

explanation.surface: Most of a dish in sauce, eaten in foreign parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 20, the answer at 20 down, ABROAD: Africa is a place abroad. Cut SSEE from FRICASSEE to leave FRICA.
explanation.definitionFit: For a British setter the continent is a foreign land, a place overseas, so it serves as an example.

clue.text: Prompter upset by cover for mathematician

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a cue prompts an actor
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A theatre prompter upset by a lid lands on a mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid of Alexandria was the Greek geometer whose Elements founded geometry, a mathematician.

clue.text: Kiss spinner at pickup point

parts.note: buss is an old word for a kiss
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: Someone kisses a spinning companion at a meeting spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside stop is where passengers are picked up by a bus, so it is a pickup point.

clue.text: Advantage securing a judge in contact with ground level

indicators.note: securing means the advantage holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: boot is an old word for advantage, as in 'to boot'
a ref, referee, is a judge of play

explanation.surface: An advantage holds a judge down at ground level.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without shoes means the soles of your feet touch the ground directly.

clue.text: Bask with leader in tabloid articles

annotationWithheld.why: Bask with leader in tabloid articles (8): SUN + B + A + THE, where B is the leader of 'Bask', which is also the definition, so one word does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Bask with leader in tabloid articles

clue.text: Cause of big bang in English tunnel, riots resulting

indicators.note: the riots result in a new order of the letters

parts.note: the plural is taken literally as two riots, riot and riot

explanation.surface: Unrest in a cross-Channel tunnel led to a big explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resulting' rearranges E, TUNNEL and RIOT RIOT; Araucaria reads 'riots' as two copies of RIOT, a liberty the solver must spot.
explanation.definitionFit: TNT, the high explosive, causes a big bang when detonated.

clue.text: See 23
Seashell or sea 20

parts.note: 20 is ABROAD, so 'sea abroad' is the French word for sea, mer

explanation.surface: A puzzle asks for a shell, or else a sea in foreign parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 refers to the answer at 20 down, ABROAD, used as a hint that the sea is to be translated into French.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is an edible ear-shaped shellfish of the Channel Islands, an abalone, so its shell is a seashell.

clue.text: Converted by the Church of England, Canary Island relocates to 3

indicators.note: relocating moves things about, so the letters of the church, canary and island are rearranged

parts.note: CE is the standard abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: An island converted by Anglicans moves its location to Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is the answer at 3 down, AFRICA. 'Converted by' merely joins the church to the fodder; 'relocates' rearranges CE plus CANARY plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyrenaica is the eastern region of Libya, so it lies in the continent the cross-reference names.

clue.text: Stirring leader's mother in hide in aircraft

indicators.note: the leader's mother sits inside the animal skin

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft

indicators.note: the hide with its contents goes inside the Russian aircraft

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin
a chief is a leader
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: The boss's mother hides in the skin of an aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring in the sense of causing trouble between people is the same as deliberate troublemaking.

clue.text: Where to land with boat as taught by Rada?

parts.note: a landing stage is where you come ashore
craft means a boat

explanation.surface: A drama school gives lessons on mooring a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, the London drama school.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical skill is what a drama academy teaches its students.

clue.text: Measure piece the wrong way, making hole in floor?

indicators.note: read the wrong way means both words are written backwards as one run

parts.note: a rood is an old measure of land area
a part is a piece

explanation.surface: Turning a measuring piece round creates a gap in the floorboards.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged flap set into a floor or ceiling is literally an opening in the floor, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Don Juan not willing to find a river 20

parts.note: loth means reluctant or unwilling
20 is ABROAD, and a river abroad in Spanish or Portuguese is rio

explanation.surface: A womaniser, reluctant, goes looking for a foreign river.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Juan is the legendary seducer, and the name of the rake in Rowe's play has become a byword for a seducer too.

clue.text: Local boss who made music

definitions.meaning: a local is a pub, and the keeper of a tavern is its boss

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an innkeeper, from tavern; the other names John Taverner, the sixteenth-century English composer.

clue.text: Jump in diamonds (no cue bid made), with no move possible

indicators.note: made reads as formed into something new from the letters

explanation.surface: At bridge someone jumps in diamonds without a cue bid and is stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jump in diamonds' also gives BOUND (jump) after ICE (diamonds), a second wordplay in the bridge surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship frozen in by ice cannot move, so it is stuck fast.

clue.text: Virtuous winner securing name with help from mentor

parts.note: guid is the Scots form of good, virtuous

indicators.note: securing means the winner holds the name inside it

parts.note: an ace is a winning serve or card

explanation.surface: A good winner gets a name with a tutor's help.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice and direction given by a mentor is what counselling or direction means here.

clue.text: Sweet arrangement of semitones with one missing

indicators.note: an arrangement rearranges the letters of the musical intervals
missing means the letter for one is dropped from the semitones before shuffling

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A musical arrangement of semitones has one note left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops I (one) from SEMITONES, leaving SEMTONES, which 'arrangement of' rearranges. The answer is a British pudding of strawberries, cream and broken meringue.
explanation.definitionFit: This pudding of crushed meringue, strawberries and cream is a classic English dessert, which British English calls a sweet.

clue.text: 3's piece at last achieves mate

indicators.note: only a piece of the cross-referenced word is kept

parts.note: 3 is the answer at 3 down, the continent Africa
at last means in the end

explanation.surface: A piece of a continent at last finds a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a pal or companion, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Une femme? Eine Frau?

parts.note: French and German for a woman; split the answer and it is a slang word for a woman with an article, and whole it means in foreign lands

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word is an American slang term for a woman with an article, and whole it means overseas, where these words are spoken.

clue.text: Move fast to deal with dead ringer in flower

parts.note: a horse canters when moving at a brisk pace
to bury is how we deal with the dead
a bell is something that rings

explanation.surface: Gallop off to see to a lookalike corpse among the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead ringer' reads as a lookalike, but 'dead' belongs with 'deal with' and 'ringer' is a bell on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: This blue or white bellflower, a campanula, is a garden plant and so a flower.

clue.text: See 18 Across
Coming to posh second match and put through the mill with climbing frame etc

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
U means upper-class, posh
a replay is a match played a second time
ground is milled, put through the mill

explanation.surface: Arriving at a smart rematch and being worn down, with gym gear about.
explanation.definitionFit: A play area with climbing frames, rope swings and the like is the outdoor space meant by the example.

clue.text: Flower unknown among old English solvers

indicators.note: among puts the unknown between the letters for old English

parts.note: x is the classic algebraic unknown
ye is an old word for you, the solvers being addressed

explanation.surface: An unknown flower turns up among veteran English puzzle solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye daisy is a large white wild daisy, so it is a flower.

clue.text: Military vehicle studied, they say, by crusader

indicators.note: they say means the words are pronounced, giving something that sounds alike

parts.note: a tank is a military vehicle and read means studied, together tank read

explanation.surface: An armoured vehicle is examined, it is reported, by a knight of the Crusades.
explanation.definitionFit: Tancred was a Norman leader of the First Crusade, so he was a crusader.

clue.text: Do a number of jewels make a fair vehicle?

parts.note: taken as written
D is the Roman numeral 500, a number
gems are jewels

explanation.surface: Asks whether a few jewels could turn into a pretty carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like beautiful but means a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumper cars at a funfair are the small electric cars of the fairground ride.
